author: hamajyotan
body:
refs #49

Objects with the same model and the same option evaluation results (e.g. `:if` or `:destroy`) will not be saved multiple times.
This is because in many cases there is no point in doing so.

```ruby
class ArModel < ApplicationRecord
  before_save { puts "saved!" }
end

class Model < ActiveRecordCompose::Model
  def initialize
    object = ArModel.new
    10.times do  # Adding the same object multiple times
      models.push(object)
      models.push(object, if: :randomize)
    end
    super()
  end

  private
  def randomize = [true, false].sample
end

model = Model.new
model.save  # "saved!" is printed only once
```

Product carousel, image carousel, accordion, pricing tables, contact forms, newsletter signup, plus 15 placeholder types in sidebar.

body: # Fix FFMPEG not working with blurays and playlists Patch or Bugfix - Bugfix ## Description Fix an issue with the `ffmpeg` support where it would not work properly on blurays that contained multiple titles in the form of playlists. The support for `ffmpeg` was introduced recently but does not take into account that transcoding titles from blurays requires the `bluray` protocol in the input file argument and the `playlist` argument for individual file transcoding. Fixes #1628 (ARM fails during FFMPEG transcode during ffprobe step when using backup RIPMETHOD_BR) ## Type of change Please delete options that are not relevant. - [X] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [X] This change requires a documentation update # How Has This Been Tested? * Tested by inserting a disc into the tray and having it get picked up by udev * Tested by running the ripper manually using `runui.py` * Tested by importing the ffmpeg module into a python3 repl and running the `run_transcode_cmd` Relevant details for my test configuration: * Uses an Intel Arc GPU for transcoding. Uses the following config values: - [X] Docker - [ ] Other (Please state here) # Checklist: - [X] My code follows the style guidelines of this project - [X] I have performed a self-review of my own code - [X] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas - [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation - [X] My changes generate no new warnings - [X] I have tested that my fix is effective or that my feature works # Changelog: Include the details of changes made here - FFmpeg support now works with blurays and playlists # Logs - Attached as a ZIP since the DEBUG level includes so much info [INCEPTION_176627213768.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24275591/INCEPTION_176627213768.zip) ## A Note on QSV Support ### Summary Below is an investigation into the correct cli (parameters) to get FFMPEG to use the Intel ARC GPU with the AV1 QSV encoder. Below uses notes from the [FFMPEG](https://trac.ffmpeg.org/wiki/Hardware/QuickSync) documentation. ### CLI Investigation The correct command for transcoding with qsv (av1) for Inception (playlist 100) - `playlist` and `-i bluray` are required to properly rip playlists from a backed up bluray. ```shell ffmpeg -init_hw_device qsv=hw -filter_hw_device hw -playlist 100 -i bluray:/home/arm/media/raw/Inception_176599407504 -vf hwupload=extra_hw_frames=64,format=qsv -c:v av1_qsv -b:v 5M -maxrate 5M '/home/arm/media/transcode/movies/Inception (2010)_176599407504/title_100.mkv' ```

# Pull Request

## Description

`OrderProcessor` was calling `dig` on `Stripe::StripeObject` instances passed from webhook events. Stripe objects only support bracket notation `[]`, not Ruby's `dig` method. This caused all webhook-triggered order processing to fail with `NoMethodError`.

Additionally, the `format_address` method was producing malformed addresses with extra commas when optional fields like `line2` or `state` contained empty strings.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)

- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Dependency update
- [ ] Performance improvement
- [ ] Security fix

## Related Issues

Fixes HoneyBadger fault #125711440

## Changes Made

**OrderProcessor** (`app/services/order_processor.rb`)
- Replaced `dig` with safe bracket notation in 5 methods:
  - `billing_address`: `@stripe_session['customer_details']&.[]('address')`
  - `shipping_address`: `collected_information['shipping_details']&.[]('address')`
  - `shipping_name`: `collected_information&.[]('shipping_details')&.[]('name')`
  - `shipping_cost`: `@stripe_session['shipping_cost']&.[]('amount_total')`
  - `shipping_id`: `@stripe_session['shipping_cost']&.[]('shipping_rate')`
- Fixed `format_address` to filter out empty strings in addition to nil values: `.compact.reject(&:empty?).join(', ')`

**Test Coverage** (`test/services/order_processor_test.rb`)
- Added 14 unit tests using `Stripe::StripeObject.construct_from()` for realistic mocks
- Coverage: customer data extraction, address formatting, edge cases, nil handling
- Helper methods to generate test Stripe session objects

**Documentation** (`BUGFIX-SUMMARY.md`)
- Technical details, before/after code comparison, verification strategy

```ruby

address = @stripe_session.dig('customer_details', 'address')

# After - works with Stripe::StripeObject
address = @stripe_session['customer_details']&.[]('address')

# Before - includes empty strings in output
.compact.join(', ')
# "123 Test St, , London, , SW1A 1AA, GB"

# After - filters empty strings
.compact.reject(&:empty?).join(', ')
# "123 Test St, London, SW1A 1AA, GB"
```

## Testing

- [ ] Integration tests added/updated

4. Verify no `NoMethodError` raised and data extracted correctly

body: ## Summary Add a complete React dashboard frontend for monitoring Amelia workflows. The dashboard uses Vite + React + TypeScript with shadcn/ui components and integrates with the FastAPI backend via static file serving. ## Changes ### Added - **Dashboard infrastructure** (Vite 6, React 19, TypeScript 5, Tailwind v4) - **shadcn/ui components** with Radix UI primitives (Badge, Card, Button, Progress, Skeleton, Tooltip, Alert, Collapsible, ScrollArea) - **ai-elements components** for agentic UI patterns (Queue, Confirmation, Loader, Shimmer) - **React Router v7** with lazy loading, error boundaries, and data router patterns - **Design tokens** with OKLCH color space and aviation theme (dark backgrounds, gold accents) - **TypeScript types** mirroring Python Pydantic models for API compatibility - **FastAPI static file serving** with SPA fallback routing - **Layout component** with sidebar navigation, connection status indicator - **Page scaffolds** for Workflows, WorkflowDetail, History, and Logs views - **Error boundaries** with RootErrorBoundary and ConnectionLost components - Unit tests for static file serving and SPA routing ### Changed - Updated server main.py to mount dashboard assets and handle SPA routing - Improved docstrings with Google-style format across several modules ### Removed - Unused BrowserCheck component and Next.js "use client" directives - Stale retry logic tests and types ## Motivation Amelia needs a visual interface for monitoring workflow execution, viewing task DAGs, and observing agent interactions in real-time. This PR establishes the dashboard foundation with: 1. A modern React stack optimized for real-time updates 2. Reusable UI components following shadcn patterns 3. Fixes #10912

Docker builds with Bun were failing because `import(\`file:${configPath}\`)` creates invalid URLs like `file:/app/...` instead of `file:///app/...`. Node.js was lenient about this, but Bun correctly rejects it.

```typescript
// before
import(`file:${configPath}`)

// after  
import(pathToFileURL(configPath).href)
```

Added tests to cover the fix.
